headline: Computational methods for spatial, single-cell, and multi-omics gene analysis
label: Omics Data Infrastructure Tools
summary: Recent papers and preprints package gene set, network, and spatial transcriptomics methods into benchmarked, reproducible computational workflows.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational method development for omics data, with most items presenting new statistical or machine learning frameworks rather than shared biological findings. Spatial transcriptomics is prominent: spaGSE applies a Bayesian hierarchical gene set enrichment model with spatial dependence, ISON predicts spot-level chromatin accessibility by integrating spatial and single-cell multiome data, and ReconST selects targeted gene panels with a gated autoencoder trained on scRNA-seq references. Enrichment methodology appears in inGSEA, which uses an Anderson-Darling weighted integral score with Cauchy combination and gamma-approximated nulls, and in markeR, an R toolkit for benchmarking gene sets as senescence markers across RNA-seq and GTEx data. Network inference is addressed by a dual-channel graph convolutional network for single-cell regulatory networks, a Gaussian copula model for multi-omics partial correlation networks, and ExIR, a reference-free framework for ranking drivers and biomarkers. ProteoForge extends imputation-aware analysis to differential proteoform discovery in proteomics. What is new is largely methodological, with several items incorporating prior knowledge or reference data, or designing explicitly for reference-free or imputation-aware analysis.
